definitions.explanation: The act of submitting a price or proposal in a competitive process, typically for government contracts, construction projects, or auctions.

examples.japanese: ⟦{公開|こうかい}→公開：11665_koukai⟧{入札|にゅうさつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{行|おこな}う→行う：01238_okonau⟧。
examples.english: To hold an open bidding process.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{工事|こうじ}→工事：00244_kouji⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{入札|にゅうさつ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{業者|ぎょうしゃ}→業者：13130_gyousha⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{決|き}める→決める：00858_kimeru⟧。
examples.english: The contractor for this construction project will be decided through bidding.

examples.japanese: ⟦{三|さん}→三：00749_san⟧⟦{社|しゃ}→〜社：04660_sha⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{入札|にゅうさつ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{参加|さんか}した→参加する：25408_sankasuru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{最|もっと}も→最も：01736_mottomo⟧⟦{安|やす}い→安い：00464_yasui⟧⟦{価格|かかく}→価格：00147_kakaku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{提示|ていじ}した→提示する：26842_teijisuru⟧⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{落札|らくさつ}⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Three companies participated in the bidding, and the company that offered the lowest price won the bid.

notes:
The formal process of submitting competitive bids, especially for public contracts. Composed of {入|にゅう} (enter/submit) + ⟦{札|さつ}→札：02153_satsu⟧ (card/slip — here referring to the bid document). Often used as a ⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ verb: {入札|にゅうさつ}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {入札|にゅうさつ}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to submit a bid
- {入札|にゅうさつ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{参加|さんか}する→参加する：25408_sankasuru⟧: to participate in bidding
- ⟦{公開|こうかい}→公開：11665_koukai⟧{入札|にゅうさつ}: open/public bidding
- ⟦{競争|きょうそう}→競争：01388_kyousou⟧{入札|にゅうさつ}: competitive bidding
- ⟦{指名|しめい}→指名：12868_shimei⟧{入札|にゅうさつ}: invited bidding (restricted to selected firms)
- {入札|にゅうさつ}⟦{価格|かかく}→価格：00147_kakaku⟧: bid price

RELATED WORDS:
- {落札|らくさつ}: winning a bid — the successful bidder
- {開札|かいさつ}: opening of bids
- ⟦{談合|だんごう}→談合：09023_dangou⟧: bid-rigging — illegal collusion among bidders

CULTURAL NOTE:
Public {入札|にゅうさつ} is a key process in Japanese government procurement. ⟦{談合|だんごう}→談合：09023_dangou⟧ (bid-rigging) has been a recurring scandal in Japanese public works, leading to stricter regulations.
